bull.b: Broad-based loan and deposit expansion shows the combined franchise is gaining client balances rather than relying on a narrow growth source. Continued balance-sheet growth can support recurring net interest income and deepen relationships, while management’s maintained guidance indicates momentum is expected to persist.

Growth across banking fees, wealth management and capital markets provides revenue diversification beyond lending spreads. This mix can make earnings more resilient when net interest margins are pressured, while expanding fee capabilities may strengthen client relationships and support durable revenue synergies.

bull.t: Strong credit quality and rising capital
bull.b: Low charge-offs and non-performing assets indicate that current growth is being achieved without broad portfolio deterioration. Simultaneously improving CET1 capital while funding loan expansion strengthens loss-absorption capacity and supports continued growth toward management’s 10.25% target.

bear.b: Expected HQLA investment and greater use of wholesale funding can raise the cost of supporting the balance sheet faster than asset yields improve. Persistent margin pressure would constrain net interest income growth and could offset some benefits from expanding loans and deposits.

Merger expenses remain large relative to quarterly earnings and are still tracking toward substantial full-year costs. Although integration may create future synergies, continued conversion spending can suppress reported profitability and reduce the near-term benefit of operating improvements.

Higher leverage combined with a lower return on equity indicates a weaker current risk-return profile than in prior periods. This can limit financial flexibility, increase sensitivity to funding and credit conditions, and make it harder for balance-sheet growth to translate into stronger shareholder returns.
